'''Zachary Norvell Jr.''' (born December 9, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Golden State Warriors]] and both of their [[NBA G League]] affiliates. He is currently an assistant coach for Gonzaga.

==Early life==
[[File:20150221 Jalen Brunson fast break.JPG|thumb|left|Norvell chasing [[Jalen Brunson]] in 2015]]
Norvell is the son of Tonja Hall and Zachary Norvell, who played basketball in college at [[Northeastern Illinois Golden Eagles men's basketball|Northeastern Illinois]] (until the program was disbanded in 1998) and [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] and coaches at [[DuSable High School]]. Growing up, the younger Norvell was an accomplished baseball player but decided to quit to focus on basketball. At [[Simeon Career Academy]], Norvell played limited minutes as a freshman behind [[Jaylon Tate]] and [[Kendrick Nunn]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kane |first1=Colleen |title=Simeon All Access Spotlight's on Zack Norvell |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/ct-spt-0228-prep-bkb-simeon-spotlight-norvell-20130227-story.html |access-date=July 4, 2018 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=February 27, 2013}}</ref> As a junior, Norvell averaged nearly 13 points, four rebounds and three assists per game and was a ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' All-State special mention selection in 2015. He played some time at point guard due to injury problems. He scored 53 points in an AAU game for Mac Irvin Fire in Las Vegas in July 2015, increasing his recruiting stock. Norvell ended up committing to Gonzaga, choosing the Bulldogs over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Narang |first1=Bob |title=Boys hoops: Simeon guard Zachary Norvell commits to Gonzaga |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/highschool/ct-spt-1103-prep-bkb-simeon-norvell-gonzaga-20151102-story.html |access-date=July 4, 2018 |work=Chicago Tribune |date=November 2, 2015}}</ref> Norvell was No. 76 in ESPN's Top 100 rankings and was nominated for the [[McDonald's All-American Game]].<ref name=Meehan/>

==College career==
Norvell underwent leg surgery before arriving at Gonzaga for his freshman season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gonzaga's depth already being tested|author=Meehan, Jim|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2016/nov/03/gonzagas-depth-already-being-tested/|date=November 3, 2016|access-date=July 1, 2018|work=The Spokesman-Review}}</ref> Norvell redshirted during his first season at Gonzaga, partially so he could recover from his leg injury.<ref name=Meehan>{{cite web|title=Gonzaga redshirt Zach Norvell Jr. maintains positive attitude, work ethic|author=Meehan, Jim|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/feb/07/gonzaga-redshirt-zach-norvell-jr-maintains-positiv/|date=February 7, 2017|access-date=July 1, 2018|work=The Spokesman-Review}}</ref> Despite his redshirt, he was allowed to play an exhibition game against [[West Georgia Wolves men's basketball|West Georgia]], where he was able to score 18 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zags cruise past West Georgia Wolves in exhibition game|author=Meehan, Jim|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2016/nov/05/zags-cruise-past-wolves-in-exhibition-game/|date=November 5, 2016|access-date=July 1, 2018|work=The Spokesman-Review}}</ref>

Coming into his redshirt freshman season, Norvell was named to the Julius Erving Award watch list.<ref>{{cite web |title=0 Zags Norvell Jr. named to Julius Erving Award watch list |url=http://www.khq.com/story/36631247/zags-norvell-jr-named-to-julius-erving-award-watch-list |website=KHQ |access-date=July 4, 2018 |archive-date=November 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105141103/http://www.khq.com/story/36631247/zags-norvell-jr-named-to-julius-erving-award-watch-list |url-status=dead }}</ref> During his redshirt freshman season, Norvell was able to become a breakout star of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], leading his team by scoring 21.5 points per game during the first 2 games of the tournament.  He was also able to make a game tying three-pointer against [[UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball|UNC Greensboro]] and recorded his first career double-double against [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] with 28 points and 12 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gonzaga's Zach Norvell Jr. has found his sweet spot during the first two games of the NCAA tournament|author=Bolch, Ben|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-ncaa-west-regional-20180321-story.html|date=March 21, 2018|access-date=July 1, 2018|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> On the season, Norvell averaged 12.7 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game. He was named West Coast Conference Newcomer of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baker |first1=Matt |title=March Madness Sweet 16: Breaking down Florida State-Gonzaga |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/fsu-seminoles/2018/03/19/march-madness-sweet-16-breaking-down-florida-state-gonzaga/ |access-date=July 4, 2018 |work=Tampa Bay Times |date=March 19, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Lakers (2019)===
Norvell went undrafted during the [[2019 NBA draft]]. On July 1, 2019, Norvell signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to a two-way contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers Sign Zach Norvell Jr. to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-zach-norvell-jr-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 2, 2019}}</ref> On October 25, 2019, Norvell made his debut in NBA, coming off from bench in a 95–86 win over the [[Utah Jazz]] with a rebound.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160667|title=LeBron scores 32, AD adds 21 in Lakers' 95-86 win over Jazz|date=October 25, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref> Norvell was waived on December 11, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title= Lakers Sign Devontae Cacok to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-devontae-cacok-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 11, 2019}}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers (2019–2020)===
On December 17, 2019,  Norvell was acquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Acquire Zach Norvell Jr.|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-zach-norvell-jr|date=December 17, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 17, 2019|archive-date=December 18, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218045125/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-zach-norvell-jr/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Norvell averaged 15.2 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.0 assists in his 29 appearances (17 starts).<ref name=WN/>

===Golden State Warriors (2020)===
On February 8, 2020, Norvell signed a 10-day contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guards Zach Norvell Jr. and Jeremy Pargo to 10-Day Contracts|url= https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/pargo-norvell-10day-contracts-20200208|date=February 8, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref> Although he had appeared in a pair of games for the Lakers,<ref name=WN>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2875425-warriors-news-zach-norvell-jr-jeremy-pargo-sign-10-day-contracts-with-gsw|title=Warriors News: Zach Norvell Jr., Jeremy Pargo Sign 10-Day Contracts with GSW|access-date=February 10, 2020|date=February 8, 2020|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|author=Daniels, Tim}}</ref> Norvell scored his first points on February 8, when he posted seven points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 17-minute [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus]] 10 debut for the Warriors against the [[2019-20 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/gameday/20200208/recap|title=New-Look Warriors Battle in Loss to Lakers: Andrew Wiggins Scores 24 Points in his Warriors Debut|access-date=February 10, 2020|date=February 8, 2020|publisher=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-zach-norvell-looks-good-in-team-debut/|title=Warriors' Zach Norvell: Looks good in team debut|access-date=February 10, 2020|date=February 9, 2020|work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2020–2021)===
On February 21, 2020, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] announced that they had acquired Norvell from the [[South Bay Lakers]] for the returning right to [[Juan Toscano-Anderson]] and a 2021 1st-round draft pick in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|2021 NBA G League Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Acquire Zach Norvell Jr In Trade|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/warriors-acquire-zach-norvell-jr-in-trade|date=February 21, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 21, 2020|archive-date=February 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200222062144/https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/warriors-acquire-zach-norvell-jr-in-trade/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his debut for Santa Cruz, Norvell scored a career-high 34 points shooting 7-of-12 from behind the arc while also contributing five rebounds and four assists in a 128–122 loss to the South Bay Lakers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Seimas |first1=Jim |title=Zach Norvell Jr. shines in Santa Cruz debut, but Warriors go flat late |url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2020/02/26/zach-norvell-jr-shines-in-santa-cruz-debut-but-warriors-go-flat-late-g-league-basketball/ |access-date=May 18, 2020 |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=February 26, 2020}}</ref>

On November 26, 2020, Norvell signed a one-year contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schaefer |first1=Rob |title=Report: Bulls Agree With Free Agent Guard Zach Norvell Jr. on One-Year Deal |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/sports/nbcsports/report-bulls-agree-with-free-agent-guard-zach-norvell-jr-on-one-year-deal/2381053/ |access-date=November 26, 2020 |work=NBC Chicago |date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> He was waived at the conclusion of training camp.

On January 12, 2021, Norvell was included in roster of [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] which would participate the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2020–21 season]] in the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] of [[Walt Disney World|Walt Disney World Resort]] located near [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2020-21-roster|title=Santa Cruz Warriors announce 2020-21 roster|date=January 12, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 12, 2021}}</ref> He was released on February 17, 2021, after suffering a season-ending injury.

==Coaching career==
Norvell returned to the [[2022–23 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team]] to serve as a student assistant and complete his degree.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/zach-norvell-jr-returning-gonzaga-020500985.html|title=Zach Norvell Jr. returning to Gonzaga as student assistant, plans to complete degree|accessdate=May 17, 2025|date=October 6, 2022|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|author=Lawson, Theo}}</ref> He became a full-time assistant coach for the [[2023–24 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/gonzaga-mens-basketball-designates-zach-norvell-jr-jorge-sanz-to-assistant-coach-roles|title=Gonzaga men's basketball promotes Zach Norvell Jr., Jorge Sanz to assistant coach roles|accessdate=May 17, 2025|date=September 22, 2023|publisher=[[SI.com]]|author=Forsman, Cole}}</ref>
